title: Session-coordinated shadow promotion with rollback playbook
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds a session-aware promotion path from shadow to canary with automated rollback triggers and an operational playbook. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context & motivation: customers running shadow traffic into new model variants frequently see noisy short-lived regressions that are hard to correlate with session state (sticky sessions, multi-request flows). This PR implements a session-coordinated promotion path: when a model variant shows stable behavior on shadowed sessions for a configurable observation window, we automatically promote a controlled subset of those same sessions into a canary lane rather than random users. The goal is to reduce promotion flakiness, increase signal fidelity for multi-request flows, and provide deterministic rollback hooks when regressions emerge.

Design summary: 1) Session fingerprint capture: the shadow bridge records a compact session fingerprint (hash of session-id, user-metadata-sanitized, request-seed) in the shadow telemetry blob; fingerprints are stored in the short-lived promotion cache (TTL configurable, default 10m). 2) Promotion eligibility: a variant becomes eligible for session-promotion after meeting coverage and success thresholds on shadowed sessions (configurable metrics: per-session success rate, median latency, absence of catastrophic errors). 3) Controlled promotion: eligible session fingerprints are used to seed canary routing so those same sessions are routed to the candidate variant (seeded canary allocation) keeping session affinity intact across multi-request flows. 4) Safety gates & rollback: we wire automatic rollback triggers (latency delta > 30% p50, error rate spike > 1.5x baseline, regression on key quality evals). When a trigger fires we immediately 1) pause new promotions, 2) drain candidate variant from promoted sessions, 3) escalate via the embedded rollback playbook (automated notifications, runbooks with one-click revert in Console). 5) Observability: new telemetry tags (session_promoted=true/false, promotion_reason, promotion_window_id) and per-session traces for promoted flows.

Configuration: new API in rollout policy: "promotion_mode: session_promote", keys: observation_window, session_ttl, min_session_coverage, success_thresholds, rollback_triggers, promotion_rate.

Migration and compatibility: default behavior is off. Operators can opt-in at rollout creation; we also include a CLI migration helper to convert existing canary definitions to session-promote-enabled templates.

Testing & safety: unit tests for controller logic, integration tests simulating multi-request flows, and a canary-sim harness that runs 10k synthetic sessions with injected latency/error faults to validate rollback conditions. We added a small staged e2e run on perf-canary lab.

Implementation notes: primary implementation lives in serving/orchestrator/promotion_controller.go and serving/bridge/shadow_bridge.go; a light-weight cache backed by redis (configurable to in-memory for dev) stores session fingerprints; telemetry is emitted via observability/telemetry_v2.

Backwards compatible: other rollout modes unchanged. Related: builds on ENG-7812 (shadow telemetry pipeline) and ENG-7824 (canary routing seeds).

Motivation story: this surfaced during a customer incident where a model change was promoted globally after shadow metrics looked stable, but multi-request checkout flows failed only for sessions that had been shadowed; session promotion reduces that risk by promoting the same sessions that were exercising the flow.

Rollout plan: 1) land as a feature-flag off, 2) enable in internal staging and run 72h synthetic session run, 3) enable for a small set of customers via Dedicated testing, 4) open opt-in in Console and document playbook.

Risks & mitigations: fingerprint collisions addressed with 128-bit HKDF-based fingerprints plus per-window salt; privacy: no PII is stored and we provide a built-in sanitizer for common identifiers; operational complexity: promotion cache TTL defaults conservative.

Ask from reviewers: please validate the rollback thresholds, the runbook phrasing, and the upgrade path for Private deployments.
commits_summary: 5 commits: 1) add promotion controller and session fingerprinting, 2) integrate promotion cache with shadow bridge, 3) telemetry and trace tags for promoted sessions, 4) rollout policy schema + CLI migration helper, 5) tests and runbook docs. Each commit scoped and unit-tested.
review_discussion: Jordan Li: Left a few nits on the promotion cache size and TTL — suggest default TTL 10m rather than 5m. Ava: updated in commit 3 to 10m and added config knob.

Priya Desai: Can you enumerate the exact metrics and query expressions used for success_thresholds? Need them for alert alignment. Ava: added exact counters (request.success_count, request.latency_p50_ms) and example PromQL in docs; please re-review.

Ethan Brooks: Do we have a clear privacy review? Fingerprinting could be sensitive. Ava: yes — the sanitizer is pluggable and defaults to hashing only non-PII fields; also filed a privacy check ENG-7901 for an audit; included mention in docs.

Jordan Li: Approved after TTL and PromQL changes. Priya Desai: Approved with one follow-up to add a Console toggle in a subsequent PR. Ethan Brooks: Approved — left a suggestion to add telemetry cardinality caps (won't block).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge on 2026-02-22. Merge commit: b7c3e1a9f4d2ea5c8a12d1b9c9f4a2d6e7b8c9f0. Release note referenced and feature gated behind 'session_promotion' flag in Console.
notes_for_ops: After deploy: monitor promotion_rate, promoted_session_error_ratio, promoted_session_latency_delta. Default rollback thresholds are conservative; if you plan to enable at scale, prewarm the promotion cache or set session_ttl to match client session behavior.
